chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muawiya ibn Hakam, from Abu Malik al-Hadrami, from Abu al-Jaroud, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Why did Allah prohibit the wine?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He prohibited it due to its effects and its spoiling.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Allah prohibit wine according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *'illa* (effective cause) by linking the prohibition of wine directly to its intoxicating effects (*ta'thir*) and the resulting corruption of the mind. This reasoning serves as the basis for the Shia juristic methodology of *qiyas* (analogical deduction), allowing scholars to extend the prohibition to any substance that produces similar intoxication, regardless of its source or name. The Imam’s concise answer highlights that the essence of the prohibition lies in the functional impact on human faculties rather than the specific type of beverage.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muawiya Bin Hukeym, from Abu Malik Al Hazramy, from Abu Al Jaroud who said,
‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Why did Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Prohibit the wine?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He<sup>azwj</sup> Prohibited it due to its effects and its spoiling’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Mu’awiyah ibn Hakim from abu Malik al-Hadramiy from abu al- Jarud who has said the following: “
I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Why Allah has prohibited wine?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He has prohibited it because of what it does and its destructive effects.’”
